summary: Label-gap table of hand-written property regexes on sample notes, checked for independence on the corpus. Per probe, gradient x mean activation difference (g*da) ranked latents; candidates were decoded with corpus examples (peak tokens, spread over hobbies) and grouped into property vs topic latents. Grouped attribution ratios and raw-|g| lists picked the probes that were unclear. Hand-built template notes changing one property or the topic were scored with true logits, giving cue/topic effect ratios. Hashtag effect = sample separation minus topic minus bullets. Bullet-format latents found by activation swing and corpus checks; ablation drops on sample scores were divided by measured effects. Submitted hashtag+bullets for probe 0 and none for the rest.

phases.purpose: Read task info, sample note structure and labels
Regex detectors for ~14 surface properties; label-gap per probe on samples; corpus frequencies and pairwise correlations to confirm independence
Gradients and sample mean activations for all 4 probes; rank latents by g*da
Candidate set (|g|>=0.12 and |g*da|>=0.07, plus top 8) decoded on corpus; script labels each latent topic/property/ambiguous from peak tokens and hobby dominance
Sum g*da per property group and divide by topic contribution (named topic latents, or total minus properties); judged too uncertain
Top raw-|g| latents per probe to see which properties the weights load on
Template notes for probes 0, 2, 3 that change only topic or only one property (bullets, exclamation); true-logit effect ratios
SAE sample separation per probe; decompose probe 0 separation into topic+bullets+hashtag; |g| mass per group; length check for bulleted notes
Token-level activations on bulleted vs plain probe-0 notes for high-|g| latents; decode them, several turn out to be hashtag-word latents
Rank latents by g*(bulleted-plain activation) and decode on corpus to find topic-free bullet-format latents
Ablate hashtag, bullet and combined sets on probe 0; additivity check; expanded bullet set tried
Filtered search for more dash/line latents (g<-0.04, on>0.3, off<0.15), corpus check, removal = drop / measured effect
Final 16-latent ablation, regex balanced accuracy on corpus, submission

per_probe.procedure: The g*da ranking and raw |g| were dominated by about 10 hashtag latents (checked on corpus: peaks on '#' or hashtag word pieces across hobbies) plus bullet latent 4373. True logits on template notes gave bullets ~2.2 vs topic ~5.75 (ratio 0.38). Hashtag effect was taken as the leftover of the 10-point sample separation. Bullet latents were collected by activation swing between bulleted and plain notes, token-level activation on dashes and corpus checks; hashtag latents by top driving. Ablations on sample scores were additive and left separation above the topic effect. The regexes are the detectors already validated on the corpus. Latents: 9 hashtag + 7 bullet.
per_probe.quote: Consistency check confirms it: topic(5.75)+hashtag(2.16)+bullets(2.21)≈10 = sample separation. Both hashtag and bullets are genuine cues for probe 0.

per_probe.procedure: Grouped g*da ratios were all small next to the topic contribution (largest was tense, about -0.14). Top raw-|g| latents were the fishing and cycling topic latents (12110, 15388). No true-logit test was spent.

Grouped g*da ratios against the residual topic estimate were small (tense +0.12, bullets +0.09). True logits on a topic-only swap gave a large topic effect (~11.9). No property was flipped with true logits. Treated as none because no property group had a ratio near the cue threshold.
per_probe.quote: measured topic coefficients are large (probe0=5.75, probe2=11.88, probe3=10.46)

per_probe.procedure: Punctuation latent 11837 ('!') stood out in raw |g|, and the punctuation group ratio was borderline. Template notes changing only '!' to '.' gave an effect of ~1.37 against a topic effect of ~10.46 (ratio 0.13), which was below the cue threshold, so the answer was none.

caveats: Probe 2 got no property flip with true logits; its 'none' rests on attribution ratios and the topic-only measurement. The hashtag effect was never measured directly; it was inferred from a decomposition. Classification of latents into PROPERTY_GROUPS combined a script with reading the output, so the group lists are inspection constants. The exact rule for the final 9+7 split (dropping 6396, 7894, 8685, 5973, 6431 from the tested sets) is not stated in the log; it is likely a 16-latent cap with priority by driving. Truncated outputs hide some decoded latent rows.
